mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4.5% in a month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a pre-tightening period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 4.5% in any month during the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 4.5% predicts negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns as higher labor market disengagement reduces consumer and business confidence.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises above 4.5% in a month
regime_hint: High unemployment or weak wage growth
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or UNRATE remains below 4.5% throughout the 60-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in HOUST (industrial production) of at least 2% for two months precedes a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak demand suppresses corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by ≥2% in two consecutive months before the horizon
regime_hint: Economic contraction or soft landing uncertainty
failure_condition: No significant drop in HOUST, or 20-day returns are positive despite the production decline.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in INDPRO above 105 (2017=100 index) for three months indicates robust manufacturing supply growth, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return via optimism about production capacity.
failure_condition: INDPRO does not exceed 105 for three consecutive months, or 20-day returns are not significantly positive.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and UNRATE both show upward trends over a 3-month window, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a positive 60-day forward return as dual accommodative signals boost risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and UNRATE both trend upward over 3 months
regime_hint: Dual accommodative policy and labor market weakness
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive, or proxies move in opposite directions.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in PAYEMS (labor market activity) below 150,000 in a month predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to reduced hiring and consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls below 150,000 in a single month
failure_condition: PAYEMS does not fall below 150,000, or 20-day returns are not negative.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in GDPC1 (GDP) of at least 2% over a 2-month period precede a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as weak demand erodes earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by ≥2% in two consecutive months
regime_hint: Economic contraction or soft landing fears
failure_condition: GDPC1 does not decline by 2% over two months, or 60-day returns are not negative.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) exceeds 700,000 for two consecutive months, it signals resilient consumer demand and supports a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as markets anticipate stronger earnings.
failure_condition: RSAFS does not exceed 700,000 for two consecutive months, or 5-day returns are not positive.
